title: Multi-time advantage for certifying quantum coherence
abstract: Non-classical dynamics in open quantum systems can be hidden in temporal correlations that are invisible to standard state- and channel-based tests. We define coherence for multi-time quantum processes and show that access to intermediate times can reveal coherence absent from all corresponding pairwise channels. Incoherent processes are fixed points of dephasing on all input and output spaces, and their coherence is quantified by relative entropy. As a proof of principle, we use an Ising model in which all three pairwise channels are incoherent while the full three-time process remains coherent. We observe this multi-time coherence on a superconducting quantum processor using a coherence witness and full process tomography.
summary: This paper introduces a concept of multi-time quantum coherence, showing that the full process history can retain quantum coherence even if all individual time steps or pairwise channels are classically mixed. By using an Ising model and superconducting QPU simulations, the authors demonstrate that memory effects across intermediate times are necessary to certify this coherence, surpassing the limitations of standard Markovian descriptions.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to certify quantum coherence in multi-time quantum processes when standard state- or channel-based tests fail to detect it.
main_result: Multi-time access to intermediate times can reveal coherence in the full process even when all corresponding pairwise channels are individually incoherent.
method: The authors define process coherence using the relative entropy of coherence and compare the full process operator to its reduced, pairwise channels.
model_or_system: The study uses an Ising model as a proof of principle and demonstrates the concept on a superconducting quantum processor (QPU) using full process tomography.
key_observables: Relative entropy of coherence ($C_{rel}$), process operators ($W$), and pairwise channel coherence.
important_parameters: The coherence is shown to persist even when individual channels are fully dephasing, contrasting with Markovian expectations.
main_assumptions: The standard description of open-system dynamics (fixed initial to later times) is insufficient, necessitating the multi-time framework.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate multi-time coherence, showing how persistent memory correlates evolution across successive time intervals, leading to coherence in the full process even if pairwise channels are incoherent.
paper_structure: The paper develops the concept of multi-time processes, defines process coherence, and then uses the Ising model (and superconducting QPU simulation) to demonstrate that non-Markovian, multi-time correlations preserve coherence when pairwise channels lose it.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the limitations of standard open quantum system descriptions by introducing a rigorous measure for coherence that captures memory effects across sequential operations, which is crucial for understanding realistic quantum computation.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic illustration of multi-time coherence. A persis- tent memory correlates the system evolution across successive time intervals, so that coherence can be present in the full multi-time pro- cess even when the corresponding pairwise channels are incoherent.

Figure 2. Relative entropy of coherence Crel(Et) of the reduced channel as a function of the dimensionless interaction time gt. The coherence vanishes whenever γ(t) = cos(4gt) cos(2gt) = 0, corre- sponding to a completely dephasing reduced channel.

Figure 3. Relative entropy of coherence (a) for the non-Markovian multi-time process and (b) for the corresponding Markovian process as functions of τ1 and τ2. The Markovian coherence vanishes when both reduced channels are incoherent, whereas the non-Markovian process retains nonzero coherence.

Figure 4. Ancilla-assisted measurement of the three-time process. Two Bell pairs retain the input and output Choi legs of the two con- secutive intervals, while the same environmental qubits E1, E2 in- teract with the system in both intervals. A SWAP at the intermediate time stores the first output and injects the second Choi probe. The four visible process legs are measured in the X basis by applying Hadamard gates followed by computational-basis measurements to evaluate the witness expectation value.
